item.title: Wau-Waria youth take first steps toward overseas jobs
item.description: The Wau-Waria Labour Mobility Hub has sent its first participant overseas, giving local youth a clear pathway to international employment. Mr Denray Demba will work abroad under approved employers in Australia and New Zealand, marking the first success for the hub since its launch in 2024 under the Wau-Waria District Development Authority’s Youth Empowerment Program. item.title: KiiiKiii makes a mark with chart-topping single ‘404 (New Era)
item.description: KiiiKiii, the newest girl group from the agency behind Ive, has rapidly climbed domestic music charts with its latest single, "404 (New Era)." Released Jan. 26 as the lead track of KiiiKiii's second EP, "Delulu Pack," the song reached No. 2 on the Top 100 chart of Melon, Korea's largest music streaming service, on Monday night. item.description: Police are preparing for crowds of up to 260,000 people at Gwanghwamun Square in central Seoul next month for a BTS comeback concert by deploying special police units and stepping up counterterrorism measures. Park Jeong-bo, the head of the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency, said at a regular press briefing on Monday that police have formed a task force led by the agency’s deputy commissioner general for public safety to oversee preparations. item.title: Vodafone’s new retail outlet in the heart of Kerema Town
item.description: To expand its reliable and affordable telecommunications services across Papua New Guinea, Vodafone PNG has opened its new retail outlet in Kerema Town, Gulf Province. Vodafone’s Public Relations Manager Charmaine ToRobert said the new container shop will provide customers in Kerema and surrounding communities with convenient access to a wide range of Vodafone products and services, including free SIM registration, mobile phones, Wi-Fi devices, vodakads, customer support, and general enquiries.

item.title: Resumption of Duties form a compulsory for all teachers
item.description: AS teachers resume their duties all throughout the country, a very important part of their teaching career is filling the Resumption of Duty Summary Sheet (RODSS) form in which all teachers must fill under the position they teach in. Head Teacher of Sotebu Primary School in the least developed Middle Ramu district of Madang province Mr Nick Bingawa said that before the next month (March), he is making sure that all his teachers are present to fill the RODSS.
